4. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Nageshshori, Kurigram, by his judgment and decree dated 20.02.2003 decreed the suit. Thereafter, an Advocate Commissioner submitted his report, against which the plaintiff-petitioners filed objection. The objection was not considered and hence the plaintiffs preferred Other Appeal No. 102 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Kurigram, who by his judgment and decree dated 20.07.2011 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 53 of 2012 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was discharged. Hence, the plaintiffs are now before us having filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 5. Mr. Bashir Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not a proper judgment in the eye of law. He further submitted that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court failed to appreciate that the plaintiffs filed the suit with a prayer for partition of their share of land measuring and area of 3.50½ acres appertaining to Plot Nos. 1381 and 1387/2036 which is his purchased property and the plaintiffs also successfully proved their title by producing documentary evidence, but the Advocate Commissioner being biased and induced by the defendants submitted report giving the plaintiffs 62 decimals land from Plot No. 1390 out of total claimed 3.50½ acres which is not his purchased property and the suit land is not a vacant land which can be possessed, so to recover the possessing of the land appertaining to plot No. 1390 measuring an area of 62 decimals will create multiplicity of litigation, therefore, the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not rejecting the Advocate Commissioner's report which is required to be interfered by this Division. He submits that the commission report gave the property appertaining to Plot No.1390 measuring and an area of 62 decimals in favour of the plaintiffs is not his purchased property and in the plaint he never claimed the property appertaining to Plot No. 1390 and this will create multiplicity of litigations because the said land is not a vacant land and as such the Courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He lastly submits that in any view of the facts, circumstances and material evidence on record the impugned judgments and decrees of the Courts below are liable to be set aside. 

 8. We note from the impugned judgment that the High Court Division found that the Advocate Commissioner prepared his report after actual physical measurement of the land on the basis of possession and title and the final decree was passed at least 4 years after the preliminary decree. Upon discussion of the judgments of the trial Court and appellate Court, the High Court Division upheld the concurrent findings of the Courts below. The finding of the Courts below is that the Advocate Commissioner rightly allocated saham to the parties. This cannot be interfered with by the High Court Division unless there was misreading or non-consideration of evidence. There was no such allegation in this case. We also note that the trial Court observed that P. W.1 stated in his deposition that he has no objection if the defendants get saham according to their claim.
